name: Spanning Tree Queries
description: You are given a connected weighted undirected graph, consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices and $$$m$$$ edges. You are asked $$$k$$$ queries about it. Each query consists of a single integer $$$x$$$. For each query, you select a spanning tree in the graph. Let the weights of its edges be $$$w_1, w_2, \dots, w_{n-1}$$$. The cost of a spanning tree is $$$\sum \limits_{i=1}^{n-1} |w_i - x|$$$ (the sum of absolute differences between the weights and $$$x$$$). The answer to a query is the lowest cost of a spanning tree. The queries are given in a compressed format. The first $$$p$$$ $$$(1 \le p \le k)$$$ queries $$$q_1, q_2, \dots, q_p$$$ are provided explicitly. For queries from $$$p+1$$$ to $$$k$$$, $$$q_j = (q_{j-1} \cdot a + b) \mod c$$$. Print the xor of answers to all queries.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$; $$$n - 1 \le m \le 300$$$) — the number of vertices and the number of edges in the graph. Each of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains a description of an undirected edge: three integers $$$v$$$, $$$u$$$ and $$$w$$$ ($$$1 \le v, u \le n$$$; $$$v \neq u$$$; $$$0 \le w \le 10^8$$$) — the vertices the edge connects and its weight. Note that there might be multiple edges between a pair of vertices. The edges form a connected graph. The next line contains five integers $$$p, k, a, b$$$ and $$$c$$$ ($$$1 \le p \le 10^5$$$; $$$p \le k \le 10^7$$$; $$$0 \le a, b \le 10^8$$$; $$$1 \le c \le 10^8$$$) — the number of queries provided explicitly, the total number of queries and parameters to generate the queries. The next line contains $$$p$$$ integers $$$q_1, q_2, \dots, q_p$$$ ($$$0 \le q_j \lt c$$$) — the first $$$p$$$ queries.
output_specification: Print a single integer — the xor of answers to all queries.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1633E — Spanning Tree Queries [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
